intro: You already know will, going to and the present continuous for the future. Today you learn to choose the right one in real situations at work and at home, to say what might happen (It might rain later), and to use the present after when, before or as soon as (I'll call you when I arrive). Warm-up: what are you doing this weekend, and what might you do?
teachingNotes: Recap, don't re-teach (the learner has done a2-will and a2-future-going-to): will = a decision made at the moment of speaking, offers, promises and opinion predictions (I think…); going to = a plan or intention decided before speaking, often with proof (tickets, paint, already paid), and predictions from what you can see now; present continuous + a future time = an arrangement fixed with another person or organisation, with a time (a meeting, an appointment, a flight, dinner at Bu Ani's). The new skill is choosing in longer adult contexts: point the learner to the clue (Did you just hear about it? Is there proof of a plan? Is it in the calendar with someone?).

Plan vs arrangement: going to and the present continuous are often both correct (I'm meeting / I'm going to meet the client on Friday). Never mark going to wrong for an arrangement, and never test going to vs present continuous as the only difference. What IS wrong: the simple present for a personal plan (common error *'Tomorrow I go to Bandung with my family' → 'Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung with my family'; Indonesian 'Besok saya ke Bandung' has no tense), will for a plan made before (*'Why the suit? — I'll have an interview' → 'I'm having / I'm going to have an interview'), and going to / present continuous for a decision made right now (*'The client is here? I'm going to go down now' → 'I'll go down now'). Timetables (The train leaves at 7) can use the simple present: accept it if the learner uses it, but don't teach it here.

might / may + base form = possibility (mungkin, about 50% or less): It might rain later. Sari may be late. Same for every subject, no to, no -s, no -ing: stress the common error *'It might to rain later' → 'It might rain later', and *'She mights come' / *'He might comes'. Negative: might not / may not (not *'don't might' or *'might won't'). Indonesian 'mungkin akan hujan' leads to *'It might will rain': English uses one of them only. might is more common in speech; may is a little more formal (emails, notices, news). maybe (a separate word, usually at the start) + will means the same: Maybe it will rain = It might rain; don't combine them ('Maybe it might rain' sounds doubled). 'May I…?' (asking permission) is a different job: mention it only if asked. Don't teach might have + past participle or could/must for guessing.

Future time clauses: after when, after, before, as soon as (= begitu / segera setelah) and until (= sampai), use the PRESENT simple even for the future; will or going to goes only in the other part (or an instruction: Call me when you arrive). Common error *'I'll call you when I will arrive' → 'I'll call you when I arrive'. It works like if in the first conditional the learner already knows (If it rains, I'll stay home). Remember -s with he/she/it (until his contract ends). Indonesian trap: 'Nanti kalau sudah sampai, kabari ya' has nanti and sudah, so learners write *'when I will arrive' or *'when I already arrive'. The present perfect is also correct in a time clause for a finished action (as soon as I've finished): accept it, but teach and test the present simple.

Don't confuse a time clause with a question: in 'When will the results come out?' when is a question word asking for a time, so will is correct. Commas: a comma after the time clause when it comes first (After I finish my shift, I'll go to the gym); none when it comes second. until + a negative main part: We won't start until Pak Hasan arrives = we start only when he arrives (Indonesian 'kita baru mulai setelah…').

Limits: no future continuous (will be doing), future perfect, shall, second conditional, passive or reported speech. Use B1 adult contexts: office meetings and clients, KRL and MRT, ojek online, family events in Bandung or Jogja, job interviews, reunions, prices in rupiah.

keyPoints.title: will, going to or present continuous? Read the clue
keyPoints.explanation: Decided right now (an offer, a promise, an answer to a problem you just heard about) → will. A plan from before, often with proof (tickets, forms, already paid) → going to. Fixed with another person, with a time (a meeting, an appointment, a flight) → present continuous; going to is also fine there. The simple present is for habits, not for your plans: Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung, not 'Tomorrow I go to Bandung'.

examples.en: Your bag looks heavy. I'll carry it.
examples.id: Tasmu kelihatan berat. Saya bawakan, ya.

examples.en: I've got the forms. I'm going to apply for the job.
examples.id: Formulirnya sudah ada. Saya mau melamar pekerjaan itu.

examples.en: We're having a meeting with the client at 10 on Monday.
examples.id: Senin jam 10 kami ada rapat dengan klien.

id.title: will, going to atau present continuous? Lihat petunjuknya
id.explanation: Diputuskan saat itu juga (menawarkan bantuan, berjanji, menjawab masalah yang baru kamu dengar) → will. Rencana dari sebelumnya, sering ada buktinya (tiket, formulir, sudah dibayar) → going to. Sudah diatur dengan orang lain, ada jamnya (rapat, janji temu, penerbangan) → present continuous; going to juga boleh di sini. Present simple untuk kebiasaan, bukan untuk rencanamu: Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung, bukan 'Tomorrow I go to Bandung'.

keyPoints.title: might / may + base form = maybe
keyPoints.explanation: When you're not sure, use might or may + the base form (the verb as in the dictionary), the same for every subject: It might rain. Sari may be late. No to and no -s: not 'might to rain', not 'she mights'. Negative: might not / may not. might is more common in speech; may is a little more formal.

examples.en: I might not come to the reunion.
examples.id: Saya mungkin tidak datang ke reuni.

id.title: might / may + bentuk dasar = mungkin
id.explanation: Kalau kamu tidak yakin, pakai might atau may + bentuk dasar (kata kerja seperti di kamus), sama untuk semua subjek: It might rain. Sari may be late. Tanpa to dan tanpa -s: bukan 'might to rain', bukan 'she mights'. Negatifnya: might not / may not. might lebih sering dipakai saat bicara; may sedikit lebih formal.

keyPoints.title: when / after / before / as soon as / until + present
keyPoints.explanation: In a time clause (the part that starts with when, after, before, as soon as or until and says when), use the present simple even for the future. will goes in the other part: I'll call you when I arrive, not 'when I will arrive'. In a question (When will you arrive?) will is fine.

examples.en: I'll call you when I arrive.
examples.id: Nanti saya telepon kalau sudah sampai.

examples.en: Text me as soon as the meeting ends.
We won't start until Pak Hasan arrives.
examples.id: Kita baru mulai setelah Pak Hasan datang.

id.title: when / after / before / as soon as / until + present
id.explanation: Dalam time clause (bagian kalimat yang diawali when, after, before, as soon as atau until dan menjelaskan kapan), pakai present simple walaupun membicarakan masa depan. will ditaruh di bagian yang lain: I'll call you when I arrive, bukan 'when I will arrive'. Dalam pertanyaan (When will you arrive?) will boleh dipakai.

the bank mightn't be open on saturday

independentPractice.prompt: Sari asks: 'Do you want tea or coffee?' Decide now and answer with I'll have …

we might go to bogor this weekend

expected: i'll lock the door before i leave the house
i will lock the door before i leave the house

assessment.prompt: Complete with the best future form of the verb in brackets. Your colleague: 'I'm so hungry, but I can't leave my desk until 2.' You: 'Don't worry. I ___ (get) you some nasi goreng from the canteen.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 'll get / will get (an offer you decide right now). 'am going to get' or 'am getting' = 40 (those are for a plan or arrangement from before). 'get' alone = 20. 'will to get' or 'will gets' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the best future form of the verb in brackets. Rina writes on Thursday: 'Sorry, I can't come to futsal on Saturday. I ___ (fly) to Makassar for my cousin's wedding. The tickets are in my bag!'
assessment.rubric: Correct: am flying ('m flying) or am going to fly: the trip was planned before and she has the tickets. 'will fly' = 30 (sounds like a decision made just now). 'fly' = 20 (the simple present is for habits). 'flying' or 'going to fly' without am = 50.

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: Take a jacket. It might to be cold in Lembang tonight.
acceptableAnswers: take a jacket it might be cold in lembang tonight
it might be cold in lembang tonight
take a jacket it may be cold in lembang tonight
it may be cold in lembang tonight
assessment.rubric: Correct: It might be cold in Lembang tonight (might + base form, no to). 'may be' = 100. 'to' removed but 'might is cold' = 40. 'will be cold' = 50 (correct English, but it loses the 'not sure' meaning). Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: You aren't sure. Rewrite the sentence with might: Maybe Budi won't come to the meeting.
acceptableAnswers: budi might not come to the meeting
budi mightn't come to the meeting
assessment.rubric: Correct: Budi might not come to the meeting. 'may not come' = 90 (correct, but the task asks for might). 'Maybe Budi might not come' = 70 (maybe and might say the same thing twice). 'might not to come' = 40. 'don't might come' or 'might won't come' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the verb in brackets: I'll send you the report as soon as I ___ (get) to the office.
assessment.rubric: Correct: get (present simple after as soon as, even for the future). 'will get' = 30 (no will after as soon as). 'am getting' = 30. 'got' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: We'll wait here until the rain will stop.
acceptableAnswers: we'll wait here until the rain stops
we will wait here until the rain stops
well wait here until the rain stops
assessment.rubric: Correct: We'll wait here until the rain stops (present simple after until; the rain = it → stops). 'until the rain stop' = 60 (missing -s). will also removed from the first part ('We wait here…') = 50. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Join the two sentences with after: I'll finish this report. Then I'll go home.
acceptableAnswers: i'll go home after i finish this report
i will go home after i finish this report
ill go home after i finish this report
after i finish this report i'll go home
after i finish this report i will go home
i'll go home after i've finished this report
after i've finished this report i'll go home
i'll go home after i finish the report
after i finish the report i'll go home
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'll go home after I finish this report / After I finish this report, I'll go home (present simple after after; will in the other part). 'after I've finished' = 100. 'after I will finish' = 40. Events in the wrong order ('I'll finish this report after I go home') = 20.

blocks.text:
You know three ways to talk about the future. A quick reminder:
- **will** + verb: you decide **right now** (an offer, a promise, a quick decision) or give your **opinion** (*I think…*).
- **am / is / are going to** + verb: a **plan from before**, or a prediction when you can **see the proof** now.
- **present continuous** (am / is / are + verb-ing) + a time word: an **arrangement**, fixed with another person, with a time.

The Indonesian word **akan** covers all three, and often Indonesian uses no future word at all (*Besok saya ke Bandung*). So don't translate the Indonesian: look at the situation.

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu tiga cara membicarakan masa depan. Pengingat singkat:
- **will** + kata kerja: kamu memutuskan **saat itu juga** (menawarkan bantuan, berjanji, keputusan cepat) atau memberi **pendapat** (*I think…*).
- **am / is / are going to** + kata kerja: **rencana dari sebelumnya**, atau prediksi saat kamu bisa **melihat buktinya** sekarang.
- **present continuous** (am / is / are + kata kerja-ing) + kata waktu: **janji yang sudah diatur** dengan orang lain, ada jamnya.

Kata **akan** dalam bahasa Indonesia mencakup ketiganya, dan sering bahasa Indonesia tidak memakai kata masa depan sama sekali (*Besok saya ke Bandung*). Jadi jangan menerjemahkan kata Indonesianya: lihat situasinya.

I have the paint. I'm going to paint my room on Sunday.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Besok saya ke Bandung sama keluarga* has no future word, so learners say 'Tomorrow I go to Bandung with my family'. The simple present (*I go*) is for habits (*I go to Bandung every month*). For a plan, say **Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung with my family.** Here *going to Bandung* is the present continuous of *go* (going to + a place = pergi ke), not *going to* + a verb.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Besok saya ke Bandung sama keluarga* tidak punya kata masa depan, jadi pelajar bilang 'Tomorrow I go to Bandung with my family'. Present simple (*I go*) untuk kebiasaan (*I go to Bandung every month*). Untuk rencana, bilang **Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung with my family.** Di sini *going to Bandung* adalah present continuous dari *go* (going to + tempat = pergi ke), bukan *going to* + kata kerja.

blocks.prompt: Rina has booked a villa for the whole family. Complete: Next Saturday we ___ to Puncak with Rina's family.
blocks.explain: It's an arrangement (the villa is booked), so use the present continuous: **we are going**. 'we go' is the simple present, for habits, and 'going' alone has no **are**.

id.prompt: Rina sudah memesan vila untuk seluruh keluarga. Lengkapi: Next Saturday we ___ to Puncak with Rina's family.
id.explain: Ini janji yang sudah diatur (vilanya sudah dipesan), jadi pakai present continuous: **we are going**. 'we go' adalah present simple, untuk kebiasaan, dan 'going' saja tidak punya **are**.

id.title: Tiga bentuk masa depan yang sudah kamu tahu

blocks.text:
In real conversations, ask yourself three questions:
- **Did I decide just now**, because of something I heard or saw? (a problem, a question, a menu) → **will**: *I'll send someone now.*
- **Is there a plan from before**, maybe with proof? (tickets, forms, money paid, classes started) → **going to**: *I'm going to apply for that job.*
- **Is it fixed with another person or a company, with a time?** (a meeting, an interview, a flight, a dinner) → **present continuous**: *Dimas is having an interview on Monday at 9.*

For an opinion about the future, use **I think … will**. For a prediction with proof you can see, use **going to**.

id.text:
Dalam percakapan nyata, tanyakan tiga hal ini pada dirimu:
- **Apakah aku baru memutuskannya sekarang**, karena sesuatu yang aku dengar atau lihat? (masalah, pertanyaan, menu) → **will**: *I'll send someone now.*
- **Apakah rencananya sudah ada dari sebelumnya**, mungkin ada buktinya? (tiket, formulir, sudah bayar, kelasnya sudah mulai) → **going to**: *I'm going to apply for that job.*
- **Apakah sudah diatur dengan orang lain atau perusahaan, ada jamnya?** (rapat, wawancara, penerbangan, makan malam) → **present continuous**: *Dimas is having an interview on Monday at 9.*

Untuk pendapat tentang masa depan, pakai **I think … will**. Untuk prediksi dengan bukti yang bisa kamu lihat, pakai **going to**.

blocks.prompt: Your friend: 'Do you want to watch a film tonight?' You: 'I can't. I ___ dinner with my in-laws at 7.'
blocks.explain: The dinner is fixed with other people, with a time, so use the present continuous: **I'm having dinner**. 'I have dinner' sounds like a habit (every night), and 'I'll have' sounds like you decide it just now.

id.prompt: Temanmu: 'Do you want to watch a film tonight?' Kamu: 'I can't. I ___ dinner with my in-laws at 7.' (in-laws = mertua)
id.explain: Makan malamnya sudah diatur dengan orang lain dan ada jamnya, jadi pakai present continuous: **I'm having dinner**. 'I have dinner' terdengar seperti kebiasaan (setiap malam), dan 'I'll have' terdengar seperti baru kamu putuskan sekarang.

id.title: Bentuk masa depan yang mana? Lihat petunjuknya

blocks.text:
**will** means you're sure (or quite sure). When you're **not sure**, about 50% or less, use **might** or **may** = *mungkin*.

The form is easy: **might / may + base form** (the verb as in the dictionary), the same for every **subject** (who does it: *I, Sari, the bank*):
- *It **might rain** later.* (not 'might to rain', not 'might raining')
- *Sari **may be** late.* (not 'may is')
- *He **might come**.* (not 'he mights' or 'he might comes': no -s)

Negative: **might not / may not**, with no *don't*: *I might not come.*

**might** is more common when we speak; **may** is a little more formal (emails, notices, news).

id.text:
**will** berarti kamu yakin (atau cukup yakin). Kalau kamu **tidak yakin**, sekitar 50% atau kurang, pakai **might** atau **may** = *mungkin*.

Bentuknya mudah: **might / may + bentuk dasar** (kata kerja seperti di kamus), sama untuk semua **subjek** (siapa yang melakukan: *I, Sari, the bank*):
- *It **might rain** later.* (bukan 'might to rain', bukan 'might raining')
- *Sari **may be** late.* (bukan 'may is')
- *He **might come**.* (bukan 'he mights' atau 'he might comes': tanpa -s)

Negatifnya: **might not / may not**, tanpa *don't*: *I might not come.*

**might** lebih sering dipakai saat bicara; **may** sedikit lebih formal (email, pengumuman, berita).

rows.en: It might rain later. Take an umbrella.
Sari may be late. The trains are slow this morning.
rows.id: Sari mungkin terlambat. Pagi ini keretanya lambat.

rows.en: I might not come to the reunion. I have a lot of work.
rows.id: Saya mungkin tidak datang ke reuni. Kerjaan saya banyak.

rows.en: We might go to Bali in December, but we're not sure yet.
rows.id: Kami mungkin ke Bali bulan Desember, tapi belum pasti.
rows.note: a possible plan, not decided (decided → going to)

id.note: rencana yang belum pasti (kalau sudah pasti → going to)

rows.en: The office may be closed on Friday because of the holiday.
rows.id: Kantor mungkin tutup hari Jumat karena libur.
rows.note: may in a notice: a bit formal

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *mungkin akan hujan* has two words (*mungkin* + *akan*), so learners write 'It might will rain' or 'It might to rain'. English needs just one: **It might rain.**

**maybe or might?** *Maybe* is a separate word, usually at the start, and goes with **will**: *Maybe it will rain* = *It might rain*. Don't use both together ('Maybe it might rain' says *mungkin* twice).

(*May I…?* is a different job: asking for permission, *Bolehkah saya…?*)

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *mungkin akan hujan* punya dua kata (*mungkin* + *akan*), jadi pelajar menulis 'It might will rain' atau 'It might to rain'. Bahasa Inggris cukup satu: **It might rain.**

**maybe atau might?** *Maybe* adalah kata terpisah, biasanya di awal, dan dipakai dengan **will**: *Maybe it will rain* = *It might rain*. Jangan pakai keduanya sekaligus ('Maybe it might rain' berarti bilang *mungkin* dua kali).

(*May I…?* punya tugas lain: meminta izin, *Bolehkah saya…?*)

blocks.explain: Negative: **might not** + the base form: **might not come**. might never takes *do / does*, and there's no *to* after it.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan sedang demam. Lengkapi: He ___ to the office tomorrow.
id.explain: Negatif: **might not** + bentuk dasar: **might not come**. might tidak pernah dipakai dengan *do / does*, dan setelahnya tidak ada *to*.

material.title: when I arrive, not when I will arrive

blocks.text:
A **time clause** is the part of a sentence that starts with **when, after, before, as soon as** (*begitu / segera setelah*) or **until** (*sampai*) and says *when* something happens.

When we talk about the future, **will** (or going to) goes in the **other** part of the sentence, but the time clause stays in the **present simple**: *I'll call you when I **arrive**.* The time word already shows that it's in the future, so English doesn't repeat *will*. It's the same as **if** in the first conditional you know: *If it rains, I'll stay home.*

Remember the **-s** with he / she / it: *until his contract **ends***.

Comma: put a comma after the time clause when it comes first (*After I finish my shift, I'll go to the gym.*), none when it comes second.

id.text:
**Time clause** (anak kalimat waktu) adalah bagian kalimat yang diawali **when, after, before, as soon as** (*begitu / segera setelah*) atau **until** (*sampai*) dan menjelaskan *kapan* sesuatu terjadi.

Saat membicarakan masa depan, **will** (atau going to) ditaruh di bagian kalimat yang **lain**, tapi time clause-nya tetap memakai **present simple**: *I'll call you when I **arrive**.* Kata waktunya sudah menunjukkan masa depan, jadi bahasa Inggris tidak mengulang *will*. Ini sama dengan **if** pada first conditional yang sudah kamu tahu: *If it rains, I'll stay home.*

Ingat **-s** untuk he / she / it: *until his contract **ends***.

Koma: beri koma setelah time clause kalau ia ada di depan (*After I finish my shift, I'll go to the gym.*), tanpa koma kalau ia ada di belakang.

rows.en: I'll call you when I arrive.
rows.id: Nanti saya telepon kalau sudah sampai.

rows.en: After I finish my shift, I'll go to the gym.
rows.id: Setelah shift saya selesai, saya ke gym.
rows.note: comma when the time clause comes first

id.note: pakai koma kalau time clause di depan

rows.en: Please turn off the lights before you leave.
rows.id: Tolong matikan lampu sebelum kamu pulang.
rows.note: an instruction works the same way

rows.en: As soon as the meeting ends, I'm going to have lunch.
rows.id: Begitu rapatnya selesai, saya mau makan siang.
rows.note: going to in the other part is fine too

id.note: going to di bagian lain juga boleh

rows.en: Budi will stay in Jakarta until his contract ends.
rows.id: Budi akan tinggal di Jakarta sampai kontraknya selesai.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Nanti kalau sudah sampai, kabari ya* has *nanti* (later) and *sudah* (already), so learners write 'when I will arrive' or 'when I already arrive'. English says just **when you arrive**: *Text me when you arrive.*

**until + not:** *We won't start until Pak Hasan arrives* = we start only when he arrives (*Kita baru mulai setelah Pak Hasan datang*).

**But a question is different:** in *When will the results come out?* **when** is a question word asking for a time, not a time clause, so **will** is correct.

You may also see the present perfect: *as soon as I've finished*. It's correct too; in this lesson, use the present simple.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Nanti kalau sudah sampai, kabari ya* punya *nanti* dan *sudah*, jadi pelajar menulis 'when I will arrive' atau 'when I already arrive'. Bahasa Inggris cukup bilang **when you arrive**: *Text me when you arrive.*

**until + not:** *We won't start until Pak Hasan arrives* = kita baru mulai setelah dia datang (*Kita baru mulai setelah Pak Hasan datang*).

**Tapi pertanyaan berbeda:** dalam *When will the results come out?* **when** adalah kata tanya yang menanyakan waktu, bukan time clause, jadi **will** benar.

Kamu mungkin juga melihat present perfect: *as soon as I've finished*. Itu juga benar; di pelajaran ini, pakai present simple.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Rina will look for a flat in Bandung after she ___ a job there.
blocks.explain: After **after**, use the present simple even for the future: **after she finds**. No will in the time clause, and *she* needs **-s**.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina will look for a flat in Bandung after she ___ a job there.
id.explain: Setelah **after**, pakai present simple walaupun untuk masa depan: **after she finds**. Tidak ada will di time clause, dan *she* butuh **-s**.

id.title: when I arrive, bukan when I will arrive

suggestedQuestions: Is 'I'm going to meet the client' wrong if it's in my calendar?
What's the difference between might, may and maybe?
Why can't I say 'when I will arrive'?
Why is 'When will you arrive?' correct, then?

resources.title: Talking about the future
resources.note: A grammar reference page: might/may for the future and the present after when, after and until. It also covers extra forms (will be + -ing) that aren't in this lesson.

id.note: Halaman referensi tata bahasa: might/may untuk masa depan dan present setelah when, after dan until. Halaman ini juga membahas bentuk lain (will be + -ing) yang tidak ada di pelajaran ini.

flashcards.front: Diputuskan saat itu juga: Tasmu berat? Saya bawakan.
flashcards.back: will: Your bag's heavy? I'll carry it.

flashcards.front: Rencana dari sebelumnya: Tiketnya sudah ada. Saya mau ke Bali.
flashcards.back: going to: I've got the tickets. I'm going to fly to Bali.

flashcards.front: Sudah diatur, ada jamnya: Besok jam 4 saya ke dokter.
flashcards.back: present continuous: I'm seeing the doctor at 4 tomorrow.

flashcards.front: Besok saya ke Bandung sama keluarga.
flashcards.back: Tomorrow I'm going to Bandung with my family. (not 'I go')
It might rain later. (not 'might to rain')
She might not come. / She may not come.

flashcards.front: Nanti saya telepon kalau sudah sampai.
flashcards.back: I'll call you when I arrive. (not 'when I will arrive')
as soon as … / until … + present: as soon as it stops, until he arrives

id.intro: Kamu sudah kenal will, going to dan present continuous untuk masa depan. Hari ini kamu belajar memilih yang tepat dalam situasi nyata di kantor dan di rumah, mengatakan apa yang mungkin terjadi (It might rain later), dan memakai bentuk present setelah when, before atau as soon as (I'll call you when I arrive). Pemanasan: apa acaramu akhir pekan ini, dan apa yang mungkin kamu lakukan?
suggestedQuestions: Apakah 'I'm going to meet the client' salah kalau sudah ada di kalenderku?
Apa bedanya might, may dan maybe?
Kenapa tidak boleh bilang 'when I will arrive'?
Lalu kenapa 'When will you arrive?' benar?

assessment.ff-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk masa depan yang paling tepat dari kata kerja dalam kurung. Rekan kerjamu: 'I'm so hungry, but I can't leave my desk until 2.' Kamu: 'Don't worry. I ___ (get) you some nasi goreng from the canteen.'
assessment.ff-2: Lengkapi dengan bentuk masa depan yang paling tepat dari kata kerja dalam kurung. Rina menulis pada hari Kamis: 'Sorry, I can't come to futsal on Saturday. I ___ (fly) to Makassar for my cousin's wedding. The tickets are in my bag!'
assessment.ff-3: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: Take a jacket. It might to be cold in Lembang tonight.
assessment.ff-4: Kamu tidak yakin. Tulis ulang kalimatnya dengan might: Maybe Budi won't come to the meeting.
assessment.ff-5: Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: I'll send you the report as soon as I ___ (get) to the office.
assessment.ff-6: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: We'll wait here until the rain will stop.
assessment.ff-7: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan after (dalam bahasa Inggris): I'll finish this report. Then I'll go home.
